notes: Profile: mid-market product analytics SaaS. 350 employees. EU + NA customer base with EU data residency requirements for some customers.
Current stack: OpenAI API (production prompts behind a small custom proxy). Rising per-token costs + need for reserved capacity motivated evaluation of Redwood.
Primary ask: quick migration path (Hosted API) with an OpenAI-compatible compat layer, then lift-and-shift to Dedicated reserved capacity later in Q3.
POC scope: 2-week hosted POC migrating 10 canonical prompts, run 2k queries/per prompt against production baseline; measure output parity, latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
Latency/throughput targets: p95 < 250ms for chat; sustained bursts to ~400 requests/s; batching acceptable for embeddings/reranking workloads.
Security: require SSO/SAML for admin console, SOC2 report, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS on Dedicated. Data residency for EU accounts mandatory.
POC timeline: kickoff 2026-02-15. Initial parity runs completed 2026-02-25. Mid-POC sync 2026-02-28.
POC findings: tokenizer differences produced ~6% delta in average summary length vs incumbent; reranker score distribution shifted causing top-1 change on 8% of ecomm queries.
SE action: implement tokenization mapping and introduce a small compat shim (openai->redwood header translation + consistent defaults). Proposed deterministic sampling seeds for reranking tests.
Observed regression risks: hallucination variance on a specific prompt family (release-notes summarization). Need eval harness to quantify regression rate target (<2% regression accepted by PM).
Pricing: Redwood sent hosted vs Dedicated TCO (2026-03-01). Preliminary looks favorable; finance requested 12-month commit scenarios and overage protections.
Legal/Security: DPA draft exchanged 2026-03-04. Need formal KMS integration plan for Dedicated. Security questionnaire submitted 2026-03-08 (see Drive doc).
Quote from PM: 'Need identical outputs for top 20 prompts, otherwise rollout risk — parity is non-negotiable for customers on our paid plans.'
Next steps: run EU-only canary on Hosted (customer subset) to validate residency + latency, then hardware benchmark for Dedicated (A100 vs L4-like options), followed by pricing negotiation.
Internal note: prioritize docs/snippets for OpenAI->Redwood mapping, add example prompt transforms, and include unit tests in customer's eval harness to detect regressions early.
Blockers summary: SSO config for staging, tokenization parity, KMS timeline, and final pricing approval from finance.
